title: Converting between slice and array in both directions

videos.script: Lesson 12 took a slice apart: its length, its capacity, and the array behind it. This lesson crosses the line between the two types, in both directions. {{toslice}} From an array to a slice is one short expression, and the slice shares the array. You need it whenever a function wants a slice and you are holding an array. There is one place it fails, and the compiler says why. {{toarray}} From a slice to an array is a conversion. One form copies the elements out. The other gives you a pointer into the same memory. If the slice is too short, the program stops, and you will see the message it prints. {{why}} Then the reason any of this matters. Arrays can be compared with two equals signs and used as map keys, and slices cannot. A SHA-256 checksum is an array for exactly that reason. By the end you can move between the two without copying by accident, or sharing by accident.
